coverage_summary:
Completed assigned TLS source/evidence review of the runtime present in candidate 50bc5cc1f7a8a67f2d9d4fe9f2916ba5a45ea590. Covered requiredScope labels certificate-identity, private-keys, tls-protocol, native-c-abi and sensitive-data. No actionable security finding survived source-to-sink review. This is not an execution result or release-admission decision.

Certificate identity: traced public TlsClientContext.handshake through NativeTlsProvider.createClientEngineWithTrustLocation and NativeTlsEngine.configureClientAuthentication. engine.cj:463-518 installs explicit trust, separate SNI and DNS/IP reference identity, rejects zoned IP references and enables peer verification. Native provider C:583-635 preserves X509_verify_cert for ordinary trust and pin-selected trust; C:1331-1389 installs SAN-only DNS verification, binary IP identity and required/optional client authentication. Public trust values copy their input and expose no TrustAll variant. Rejected a suspected partial-wildcard bypass after inspecting the configured pinned AWS-LC source: include/openssl/x509.h:5025-5028 documents NO_PARTIAL_WILDCARDS as an always-enabled behavior, and crypto/x509/v3_utl.c:793-845 enforces a whole first label and at least two suffix dots. The missing OpenSSL-style flag is therefore not a defect in this pinned provider.

Private keys and callbacks: examined PrivateKeyRef.pkcs8, pkcs8File, withPkcs8, snapshotForContext, close/finalizer and LocalIdentity validation in identity.cj:80-112,152-212,262-328,347-427. Context builders snapshot key material; public TLS contexts keep adopted identities and decryptor services private. Native C:1586-1706 validates and installs PKCS#8/external identities, clears previous private-operation state and respects AWS-LC key-method replacement ordering. Native C:327-429,1714-1851 bounds and copies paused callback input/results. engine.cj:999-1199 invokes signer/decryptor services outside the engine lock, rechecks operation state, converts failure to a failed native operation and zeroes transferred decryptor output in finally. The RSA_RAW contract in tls_contract.cj:168-215 leaves padding validation in AWS-LC; pinned handshake_server.cc:1337-1413 checks full block length and selects the premaster or random fallback in constant-time padding/version processing. Caller implementations remain trusted service inputs, not remotely supplied code.

SNI and resumption: server_name.cj:53-135 bounds exact routes and rejects missing/nonmatching SNI. package.cj:531-559 creates an initially unconfigured selector engine, so selected settings do not accumulate over an unrelated default context. engine.cj:759-880 installs the selected identity, ALPN, hooks, trust, protocol range and session-id context before completing selection. Pinned AWS-LC handshake_server.cc:604-635 freezes/negotiate versions after the early callback. context.cj:128-142 allocates checked unique context epochs; session.cj:16-51,223-258 includes security/trust/identity/provider/ALPN/context-version partitions. Native session offers remove early-data state; TLS early data is explicitly disabled. Pinned ssl_session.cc:452-460 compares session-id contexts. Session storage is bounded, synchronized, expires entries and clears evicted/closed bytes.

Native ABI and sensitive data: reviewed header signatures against C implementations and Cangjie bindings, DER exact-consumption checks, LONG_MAX/SIZE_MAX/INT_MAX conversions, query/copy capacities, bounded certificate chains, ALPN framing, BIO ownership and partial-construction cleanup. Native handles are internal pointer-backed handles serialized by the Cangjie provider/engine locks, not a security boundary for arbitrary forged C callers. Production keylog storage/callbacks/capability and entry points are preprocessor-gated at C:64-69,108-114,234-284,879-881,1853-1933. Builders reject unavailable capability. tools/build_linux_tls_provider.py:246-267,373-395,567-572 separates test-keylog fingerprints and output paths. Native cleanup cleanses private-operation/session/ticket material; reviewed runtime diagnostics expose typed classes/reasons rather than native error strings or key bytes. Pinned AWS-LC defaults disable renegotiation/compression and its default ALL cipher filter excludes NULL and 3DES.

Evidence comparison: the initially reviewed qualification.json, native-rebuild.json, current provider manifest and supply-chain provider sidecar agree on AWS-LC 5.5.0 commit 991e67ff4cf04df4dd89e407f8b920c6936cb56a, provider build fingerprint 08df58f75caefedf09cafd021abad011fba371a320e594867f153b0835adb707 and TLS archive digest 4d00dfdca62e62ca37193144fcf6a74c20313b79a52e203e9abc915a9a7c27e8. Manifest declares test_only_key_log=false; qualification records no OpenSSL dynamic dependency. These are inspected records, not independently rerun checks. The campaign's hostname target exercises the standalone verifier, certificate-adapter target constructs trust/engines without a completed peer handshake, and TLS record/handshake targets classify bounded mutations. They do not prove exhaustive authentication, callback or resumption correctness.

Integration owner M8ReleaseReview was notified of the completed no-finding source result and pending packet refresh. Reviewer is a process-isolated agent sharing the same assistant/provider ecosystem, not an external human or organizationally independent reviewer.

deferred.reason: Main announced tooling corrections and regeneration of qualification/fuzz/security inputs while this audit ran, with runtime .cj/native source unchanged. The last inspected review request still identified package digest 5d77eedae9c0fdb46e9dad65141c85c002dbaec8ec0dfcf19afa0c896eeaa88e. Integration owner must bind this unchanged-runtime source result to the refreshed candidate and review the refreshed packet before authoring the final independent-review.json.

No builds, tests, linters, formatters, payload execution, network calls or source edits. No independent archive-byte/hash recomputation, advisory lookup, sanitizer execution, timing measurement or exhaustive AWS-LC review. Only relevant pinned dependency functions and headers were inspected. Historical reports were not used to qualify current source.

Formal 86400-second soak, hosted signatures, non-Linux-x86_64-glibc platforms and release orchestration remain separate gates outside this slice. Absence of findings does not establish their completion.
